home.hero_title: From field notebook to publishable data
home.hero_subtitle: Padiush carries a whole ethnobotanical study: interviews and field records captured even with no signal, local names reconciled against accepted taxa, and quantitative indices with their formulas cited.
home.hero_note: Free software, in Spanish, English and Portuguese.
home.cta_contact: Write to us and tell us what you are documenting.
home.preview_caption: Real output from the platform, generated with the example study.
home.workflow_subtitle: What you record in the field is what you analyse. Nothing gets transcribed twice.
home.workflow_1_desc: Build the interview form with repeatable sections, local-name fields and use categories.
home.workflow_2_desc: The field app works with no signal. Interviews, records, location, audio and photographs stay encrypted on the phone until the network comes back.
home.workflow_3_desc: Link each reported name to an accepted taxon. The original name the interviewee used is never lost.
home.workflow_4_desc: Calculate the indices, review the charts and export to CSV, Excel or the ethnobotanyR package.
home.capture_title: It does not depend on having signal
home.capture_desc: The field app, Padiush Companion, keeps every interview and every record on the phone and sends them when a connection returns. Each one carries its own identifier, so retrying a send never duplicates data.
home.capture_point_1: Answers, GPS location, audio and photographs
home.capture_point_2: Local store encrypted with SQLCipher; the app refuses to capture if encryption is unavailable
home.capture_point_3: If the connection drops, large files pick up where they left off
home.capture_point_4: You always know when you last synced and what is still to be sent
home.records_desc: Document observations and collected specimens with coordinates, photographs and a voice note, from the phone or from the web. A record can start from an interview answer that names the plant, and stays linked to it.
home.records_point_1: Observations and collected specimens, with project accession numbers
home.records_point_2: A determination history: who identified each specimen, as what, and when
home.records_point_3: Collecting permits recorded and attached to each specimen
home.records_point_4: The answer each record came from, one click away
home.taxonomy_desc: Search World Flora Online from the species page, adopt the accepted name and keep a record of where the change came from. Distribution comes from the World Checklist of Vascular Plants through GBIF, and an iNaturalist reference photograph helps confirm the identification.
home.taxonomy_point_2: Synonyms and accepted names clearly distinguished
home.taxonomy_point_3: Native and introduced distribution by botanical region
home.taxonomy_point_4: The name reported in the field is always preserved
home.analysis_title: Quantitative indices with their formulas cited
home.analysis_desc: The classic measures of quantitative ethnobiology, calculated on your data, each with the reference that defines it and worked examples verified against the literature.
home.analysis_point_1: Tables by species and by use category, plus fidelity level
home.analysis_point_2: Bar charts, a heatmap and a use-report flow diagram
home.analysis_point_3: Download as SVG or PNG, with your choice of background and resolution
home.analysis_point_4: Export to CSV and Excel, and an informant × species matrix for ethnobotanyR
home.trust_1_desc: You keep ownership of your research. We do not sell data, we do not run advertising, and we do not train artificial intelligence models on it.
home.trust_2_desc: Answers are encrypted in the database and the phone’s store is encrypted at rest. From your account you can see which browsers and phones you are signed in on, and sign any of them out.
home.trust_3_desc: Invite collaborators with different roles: the person capturing, the person analysing and the person only consulting each see something different.
home.trust_4_desc: Who recorded what, which source a name came from, and what a value was before a correction: all of it is written down.
home.final_cta_desc: With your account you can open a copy of the example study, with interviews, records, species and indices already calculated, and explore it before you design your own. The first time you open each section, a short tour shows you how it works.

about.lead: Padiush began from an uncomfortable observation: much of the ethnobotanical knowledge documented in the field ends up scattered across notebooks, spreadsheets and files nobody opens again.
about.p1: The problem is rarely a shortage of data. It is that the path from interview to publishable result is full of manual transcription, names that do not match and calculations redone by hand. Every one of those steps loses information and adds errors.
about.p2: We built Padiush so that path is a single one. What gets recorded in front of the interviewee is the same thing that feeds the species catalog, the indices and the final export, with no intermediate spreadsheet.
about.p3: We work from El Salvador, in Spanish first, because most tools in this field are designed in English and for other contexts.
about.open_source: Padiush is free software. You can read the code that handles your informants’ data, run your own instance, or adapt it to your study:
about.how_1_desc: Every index we implement has a documented formula, a bibliographic source and a verified worked example. If we cannot cite it, we do not calculate it.
about.how_2_desc: The name the interviewee used, the source a taxon came from and the value before a correction are all kept. Data has to be auditable.
about.how_3_desc: Whoever leads the research decides what gets recorded and answers for consent. We process that information on their instructions, not our own.
